messages.subject: How can I use raster::getData in a deployed Shiny-App
messages.subject_clean: How can I use raster::getData in a deployed Shiny-App
messages.body_plain:
I am trying to deploy a Shiny-App which uses the function "getData" from the raster package.

I wrote a little example file below, which uploads and plots a shapefile.
By pressing on the Action Button "Plot Elevation", an SRTM-file should be downloaded, cropped and masked with the given shapefile
and should then be plotted.

When i run the App locally, there seems to be no error.
However, when i deploy the app, I get the "Error: file not found" when trying to plot the masked SRTM file.
I tried running the "getData"-funtion with "local", but the error remains the same.

Am I missing something?

The shiny-App example in its actual state can be seen and tested at: https://windfarmga.shinyapps.io/srtmtest/

Many Thanks in advance!!

My ui.R-File:
library(shiny)
library(raster)
library(rgdal)

source("server.R", local = T)

ui = fluidPage(
  sidebarLayout(
    sidebarPanel(
      fileInput(inputId="Shape_SHID", label = "Upload all files of a Polygon representing the area,
            where the wind farm should be optimized.",
                multiple = TRUE,accept = c('.shp','.dbf','.sbn','.sbx','.shx',".prj"))
    ),
    mainPanel(  plotOutput("SHPplot"),
                actionButton("Srtm_PLot", label = "Plot Elevation"),
                plotOutput("srtmpl"))
  )
)
shinyApp(ui, server)

My server.R-File:
library(maptools)
library(sp)
library(raster)

server = function(input, output) {

  shape <- reactive({
    req(input$Shape_SHID)
    req(!is.null(input$Shape_SHID))
    myshape<- input$Shape_SHID
    dir<-dirname(myshape[1,4])
    for (i in 1:nrow(myshape)) {
      file.rename(myshape[i,4], paste0(dir,"/",myshape[i,1]))
    }
    getshp <- list.files(dir, pattern="*.shp", full.names=TRUE)
    maptools::readShapePoly(getshp, proj4string = CRS(as.character("+proj=longlat +ellps=WGS84 +datum=WGS84 +no_def")));
  })

  output$SHPplot <- renderPlot({
    req(input$Shape_SHID)
    req(!is.null(input$Shape_SHID))
    namesInp <- input$Shape_SHID[,1]
    shiny::validate(
      need(expr = length(grep("shp", namesInp, perl=T, value=F))>0, message = "A (*.shp)-File is missing."),
      need(expr = length(grep("dbf", namesInp, perl=T, value=F))>0, message = "A (*dbf)-File is missing."),
      need(expr = length(grep("shx", namesInp, perl=T, value=F))>0, message = "A (*shx)-File is missing."),
      need(expr = length(grep("prj", namesInp, perl=T, value=F))>0, message = "A (*prj)-File is missing.")
    )
    par(bg="gray96")
    plot(shape(), col="orange")
  })

  Srtm <- eventReactive(input$Srtm_PLot,{
    Polygon1 <- shape()
    ProjLAEA = "+proj=laea +lat_0=52 +lon_0=10 +x_0=4321000 +y_0=3210000
    +ellps=GRS80 +towgs84=0,0,0,0,0,0,0 +units=m +no_defs"
    Polygon1 <-  sp::spTransform(Polygon1, CRSobj =
                                   raster::crs("+proj=longlat +datum=WGS84 +ellps=WGS84 +towgs84=0,0,0"));
    extpol <- round(Polygon1@bbox,0)[,2]

    srtm <- local(raster::getData(name = 'SRTM', download = T, lon=extpol[1], lat=extpol[2]));
    srtm_crop <- raster::crop(srtm, Polygon1);
    srtm_crop <- raster::mask(srtm_crop, Polygon1)
    Polygon1 <-  sp::spTransform(Polygon1, CRSobj = raster::crs(ProjLAEA));
    srtm_crop <- raster::projectRaster(srtm_crop, crs = raster::crs(ProjLAEA));
  })
  output$srtmpl <- renderPlot({
    Srtm <- Srtm()
    plot(Srtm)
  })
}

messages.subject: Re: Unable to show dynamic content from a module in a sidebarMenu in shinydashboard
messages.subject_clean: Unable to show dynamic content from a module in a sidebarMenu in shinydashboard
messages.body_plain:
This is a bug in shinydashboard. Shiny doesn't render outputs that it doesn't think are visible. In this case, it sees that the sidebar copy of uiOutput isn't visible, so it doesn't run the renderUI. The bug is that whenever that visibility changes, the JS is supposed to let Shiny know by doing a $(document).trigger("shown") (or "hidden") but shinydashboard appears not to be doing that.

You can work around this for now by adding below this line inside of the dynamicText function:

outputOptions(output, "dynText", suspendWhenHidden = FALSE)

And we'll file an issue on shinydashboard to get this fixed, if there isn't one already. Thanks!

       session = session,
       filePath = paste0("data/", i, ".csv"),
       readFunc = read_csv)
     }

  ##########################################

> This is a bug in shinydashboard. Shiny doesn't render outputs that it doesn't think are visible. In this case, it sees that the sidebar copy of uiOutput isn't visible, so it doesn't run the renderUI.   verbatimTextOutput("file1"),
  verbatimTextOutput("file2"),
  verbatimTextOutput("file3")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {

  file1 <- reactiveFileReader(intervalMillis = 1000,
    session = session,

    filePath = "file1.csv",

    readFunc = read_csv)

  files_to_get <- c("file2", "file3")

  other_files <- lapply(files_to_get, function(i) {
    reactiveFileReader(
      intervalMillis = 1000,
      session = session,

      filePath = paste0("", i, ".csv"),
      readFunc = read_csv)
  })

  output$file1 <- renderPrint({ file1() })
  output$file2 <- renderPrint({ other_files[[1]]() })

  output$file3 <- renderPrint({ other_files[[2]]() })

}

shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)

messages.subject: Re: How to get a shiny UI widget type at runtime
messages.subject_clean: How to get a shiny UI widget type at runtime
messages.body_plain:
I agree with Barbara, it sounds like what you want should be achievable with the bookmarking feature.

If you're really keen on getting the type of an input, you can see how shinyjs achieves that (it's needed in the shinyjs::reset() function because a different update function is called depending on the input type). It's not super straight forward code, but it is documented so if you spend half an hour looking into it you'll be able to use the same method in your own code. Relevant code: saving the type of each input using javascript: https://github.com/daattali/shinyjs/blob/master/inst/srcjs/shinyjs-default-funcs.js#L284-L392 and retrieving the input type in R https://github.com/daattali/shinyjs/blob/master/R/reset.R

There are of course other ways to achieve this, this is just an example you can try to follow

I am developing functions to use Google's Material design in shiny apps.

It appears I can write these functions in 1 of 2 ways:

#1 Using shiny tags
e.g.
materialButton <- function(inputId, label){
  shiny::tags$button(
    id = inputId,
    class = 'materialButtonClass',
    label
  )
}

#2 Generate HTML strings
e.g.
materialButton <- function(inputId, label){
  HTML(
    paste0(
             "<button",
             " id=", inputId,
             " class=", "'materialButtonClass'",
             ">",
             label,
             "</button>"
    )
  )
)

#1 seems more conventional, however #2 gives me ultimate flexibility.

My question is:
Is there an issue using shiny::HTML (#2) to create functions to generate HTML strings?

Thank you,
EA

Note:
Tags such as "button" did not cause any issues. I ran into an issue when trying to create a "materialSelectInput". Specifically, assigning which value is "selected" using only shiny tags. If I use HTML strings instead, specifying the "selected" value becomes much more simple.

messages.subject: Re: problem deploying app with mapview dependency on shinyapps.io server
messages.subject_clean: problem deploying app with mapview dependency on shinyapps.io server
messages.body_plain:
I believe that the sf and rgdal R packages are incompatible, since support for sf requires libgdal 2, which was added to the sf installer recently <https://github.com/rstudio/shinyapps-package-dependencies/pull/72>, while by default libgdal 1 is what is available.

An additional way to work around it might be by disabling the package cache for your application.

We will look into what it would take for both packages to be able to be installed together.

On Wednesday, March 8, 2017 at 10:04:27 AM UTC-6, Bárbara Borges wrote:
> Two things:
>
> The bug that I think you're looking for is that you're calling the functions modXreturn inside the callModule() call, instead of in the module server function. So if you change that, you'll see the trickling down you're expecting. Here's the working code (differences highlighted):

>   tagList(
>     uiOutput(ns("txtOut"))
>   )
> }
> mod2 <- function(input, output, session, prevModReturn){
>   output$txtOut <- renderUI(
>     h2(prevModReturn())
>   )
>   return(reactive(session$ns(prevModReturn())))
> }
>
> ui <- fluidPage(
>   fluidRow(

>         mod2UI("myMod2"),
>         mod2UI("myMod3"),

>       )
>     )
>   )
> )
>
> server <- function(input, output) {
>   mod1return <- callModule(mod1, "myMod1")
>   mod2return <- callModule(mod2, "myMod2", mod1return)
>   mod3return <- callModule(mod2, "myMod3", mod2return)
>   mod4return <- callModule(mod2, "myMod4", mod3return)
> }
>
> shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)

> This is a pretty fundamental concepts in modules and it seems to trip up a lot of people. The secret with modules is never passing actual values (in your case, the return value of the  modXreturn function), but passing in the recipe itself (in your case, the modXreturn function itself). If you pass in a value, it will never update again. If you pass in a (reactive) recipe, it will update properly.
>
>
> Are you sure you're doing what you want to do? You said:
>
> "I take the input and process it in a module and display some output (let's call it module 1), then I take the output of module 1 and process it in another module"
>
> But what you're doing above is taking the input, process it in a module and display the output (so far so good), then taking the input (not the output, like you said) and re-process it from scratch in another module. You're also using the session$ns() function in a strange way. This is usually used when you're creating dynamic inputs on the module server function. If you're just passing already-existing inputs, you don't need it... In your case, literally the only effect it is having is concatenating the module id to the string... If you don't want that, just take that out:
>
> library(shiny)
>
> mod1UI <- function(id){
>   ns <- NS(id)
>   tagList(
>     textInput(ns("txtIn"), "Enter Your Text:", "My Text"),
>     uiOutput(ns("txtOut"))
>   )
> }
> mod1 <- function(input, output, session){
>   output$txtOut <- renderUI(
>     h2(input$txtIn)
>   )
>   return(reactive(input$txtIn))
> }
>
> mod2UI <- function(id){
>   ns <- NS(id)
>   tagList(
>     uiOutput(ns("txtOut"))
>   )
> }
> mod2 <- function(input, output, session, prevModReturn){
>   output$txtOut <- renderUI(
>     h2(prevModReturn())
>   )
>   return(reactive(prevModReturn()))
> }
>
> ui <- fluidPage(
>   fluidRow(
>     column(12,
>       tagList(
>         mod1UI("myMod1"),
>         mod2UI("myMod2"),
>         mod2UI("myMod3"),
>         mod2UI("myMod4")
>       )
>     )
>   )
> )
>
> server <- function(input, output) {
>   mod1return <- callModule(mod1, "myMod1")
>   mod2return <- callModule(mod2, "myMod2", mod1return)
>   mod3return <- callModule(mod2, "myMod3", mod2return)
>   mod4return <- callModule(mod2, "myMod4", mod3return)
> }
>
> shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)
>
>
> More importantly though, if your goal is to process things in chunks (each module is responsible for a step of the processing), this is not accomplishing it, because you're just passing in the same unaltered input every time. This is what I think you were looking for:

>   )

>     h2(input$txtIn)
>   })
>

>     processedTxt()
>   )
>   return(processedTxt)
> }
>
> mod2UI <- function(id){
>   ns <- NS(id)
>   tagList(
>     uiOutput(ns("txtOut"))
>   )
> }
> mod2 <- function(input, output, session, prevModReturn){
>   processedTxt <- reactive({
>     tags$em(prevModReturn())
>   })
>
>   output$txtOut <- renderUI(
>     processedTxt()
>   )
>   return(processedTxt)
> }
>
> mod3UI <- function(id){
>   ns <- NS(id)
>   tagList(
>     uiOutput(ns("txtOut"))
>   )
> }

>
>   output$txtOut <- renderUI(

> shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)

>
>

messages.subject: Shiny app on shiny-server does not ask for ssh password
messages.subject_clean: Shiny app on shiny-server does not ask for ssh password
messages.body_plain:
Hello everyone,

So, I created a small Shiny app and I hosted it on a server, let say server A. This app will try to connect to another server, let say server B by ssh. To do this connection, I used the run.remote from package ssh.utils of CRAN.

When I try to run my Shiny app from RStudio (with the "Run App" button) directly on server A, a small window is popping up asking for the password to gain access server B.

However, when I use shiny-server on server A and run the app, I see NO pop up window asking for the password. Yet on the shiny-server log I found the following message:

Permission denied, please try again.
Permission denied, please try again.
Permission denied (publickey,gssapi-keyex,gssapi-with-mic,password).

Meaning that my app has tried three times to have access that I am not aware of.

My question is, what should I do with shiny-server so it will also pop out the window to ask password just like when I use Rstudio? Another is, I do not want to use the ssh private/public key.

The following is my simple code who lives in server A:

library(shiny)
library(shinyFiles)
library(ssh.utils)

ui <- fluidPage(
  navbarPage(title = "Main window",
             tabPanel(title = "Test SSH",
                      textInput(inputId="username", label = h3("Username:")),

                      actionButton("submit", "Submit")
             )
  )
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {

  observeEvent(input$submit, {
    res <- run.remote("randomScript",remote = paste0(input$username,"@server-b.de <http://server-b.de>"))
  })
}

shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)

Thanks beforehand.

messages.subject: Re: Git setup for Shiny
messages.subject_clean: Git setup for Shiny
messages.body_plain:
No reason not to make it the root folder. Any file you edit for your app should be in version control.

Whether or not to keep data in the repo is a judgment, in my opinion. I personally would if there's no pressing reason to keep it private, like data confidentiality, etc. Some may disagree. For a simple app, it seems fine.

If you do not think the data should be in version control, you can put the file in the .gitignore file in the root of your repo.

Erik

messages.subject: Re: How to input the "column" name in ggplot? thanks
messages.subject_clean: How to input the "column" name in ggplot? thanks
messages.body_plain:
Let's say you have a column "speed", you'd do aes(speed). But if you have a variable named x that might contain the strings "speed" or "dist", and you want the value to be used as the column, you can't do aes(x) (because that would just look for a column named "x"); instead you'd do aes_string(x), which would look at the value of x to find the column. The same works with any other values you can evaluate, so aes_string(factor(input$select1)) ought to work. (You put input on the right-hand side of the $ multiple times, that's also wrong)

messages.subject: Re: Shiny app on shiny-server does not ask for ssh password
messages.subject_clean: Shiny app on shiny-server does not ask for ssh password
messages.body_plain:
I want to have an interface that will allow users to pass some arguments/parameters to an Rscript that is located in another server, but only after these users supply their ssh credentials to this another server.

On 12 March 2017 at 01:47, Joe Cheng <j...@rstudio.com> wrote:

> What exactly is the scenario you're trying to support?
>

> On Sat, Mar 11, 2017 at 5:57 AM Wahyu Hadiwikarta <wahyu.w...@gmail.com> wrote:

> > Thanks for the response. No, I am using the free/open source version. If it is a terrible idea, do you have suggestion for other solution?
> >
> >
> > Cheers,
> >
> >
> > On Saturday, March 11, 2017 at 3:14:36 AM UTC+1, Joe Cheng [RStudio] wrote:
> > > This seems like a very terrible idea to be passing your SSH password over the wire like this. Are you using Shiny Server Pro?
> > >
> > > On Fri, Mar 10, 2017 at 1:59 AM Wahyu Hadiwikarta <wahyu.w...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > > Hello everyone,
> > > >
> > > >
> > > >
> > > > So, I created a small Shiny app and I hosted it on a server, let say server A. This app will try to connect to another server, let say server B by ssh. To do this connection, I used the run.remote from package ssh.utils of CRAN.
> > > >
> > > >
> > > > When I try to run my Shiny app from RStudio (with the "Run App" button) directly on server A, a small window is popping up asking for the password to gain access server B.
> > > >
> > > >
> > > > However, when I use shiny-server on server A and run the app, I see NO pop up window asking for the password. Yet on the shiny-server log I found the following message:
> > > >
> > > >
> > > > Permission denied, please try again.
> > > > Permission denied, please try again.
> > > > Permission denied (publickey,gssapi-keyex,gssapi-with-mic,password).
> > > >
> > > >
> > > > Meaning that my app has tried three times to have access that I am not aware of.
> > > >
> > > > My question is, what should I do with shiny-server so it will also pop out the window to ask password just like when I use Rstudio? Another is, I do not want to use the ssh private/public key.
> > > >
> > > >
> > > > The following is my simple code who lives in server A:
> > > >
> > > >
> > > > library(shiny)
> > > > library(shinyFiles)

messages.body_plain:
There are at least two problems here:

1. Inside your observeEvent, you use <- to assign to results. That will just create a local variable (scoped inside the observeEvent) called results. To assign to the results variable that's in the parent scope of observeEvent, you need to use <<- instead.

2. Simply assigning to a regular variable isn't enough to induce reactivity. You need the variable to be reactive aware. You can turn results into a reactive aware variable by calling makeReactiveBinding("results") right after you first declare it.

Hope that helps.

messages.body_plain:
There were a couple more remaining bugs.

3. When you built up the results list, it was an unnamed list--the values were not registered under [["input1"]], but as [[1]] (for example). So that's why you were getting NULL as results. If you change the `test` reactive expression to use `results[[i]]` instead of `results[[inputName]]` then that would fix it.

4. The results list doesn't contain values, but, reactive expressions. So you actually want `results[[i]]()`.

With those two fixes it works for me.

messages.subject_clean: How to use shinydashboard elements inside a shiny::fluidPage
messages.body_plain:
Below is a MRE, in case someone has any idea on how to do it. I guess, I have to include some `tag` at the beginning of the script or to wrap the output inside a specific `div`, but i'm not sure of what should I add. Thanks.

library(shiny)
library(shinydashboard)

# shiny UI
ui_s <- fluidPage(
  fluidRow(
    valueBoxOutput("BoxDown", width = 4),
    valueBoxOutput("BoxUp", width = 4)
  )
)

# shinydashboard UI
ui_db <- dashboardPage(
  dashboardHeader(),
  dashboardSidebar(),
  dashboardBody(
    fluidRow(
      valueBoxOutput("BoxDown", width = 4),
      valueBoxOutput("BoxUp", width = 4)
    )
  )
)

# server
server <- function(input, output) {
  output$BoxUp <- renderValueBox({
    valueBox(
      value = 100,
      subtitle = "Upregulated",
      icon = icon("arrow-up"),
      color = "red"
    )
  })

  output$BoxDown <- renderValueBox({
    valueBox(
      value = 50,
      subtitle = "Downregulated",
      icon = icon("arrow-down"),
      color = "olive"
    )
  })
}

# Run the shiny app
shinyApp(ui_s, server)

# Run the shinydashboard app
shinyApp(ui_db, server)

That was also my first guess. I have a RStudio addin to search all functions, symbols in all packages installed <https://github.com/dracodoc/namebrowser>. So I fired it up and checked with "span". You can see from the attachment that only libraries with "span" is htmltools, shiny and geoshpere. I tried to load library of "geosphere" first then launch the app, but there was no error.

When I first met the problem, the error message indicated that problem was with this line:

showNotification(span(icon("spinner fa-spin"), "Importing data..."), type = "message", duration = NULL)

I changed "span" into "tags$span". Then when the problem appear again, it was about a second occurrence of similar usage:

showNotification(span(icon("spinner fa-spin"), "Downloading studies..."), type = "message", duration = NULL)

So it definitely was caused by naming conflict with "span", but I'm not sure which package caused that, since I have searched all my packages. And I believe there is no variable named "span" in my global environment.

Anyway, the problem should be solved with using full qualified name. Thanks!

messages.subject_clean: actionButton in RShiny : alternative to reset value
messages.body_plain:
Thank you Joe!.

I have an other relative question.
In my case I need to use the eventReactive()function instead of observeEvent() because I want to use objects (VAL and IDX in my example) in my plot and my table. In addition I have to know if this object comes from after a click on the actionButton in order to get the right result, so I think I have to use the reactiveValues() function.
To get the results  (VAL and IDX) my plot and my table, I think that I have to put the eventReactive() and the test on the value of the reactiveValues() inside a global reactive().
But beacause of the using of reactiveValues()and reactive() it is no possible to use the actionButton:

ui <- fluidPage(
  sliderInput("Param1", label = "Param 1",

              min =  0,
              max = 10,
              value = 0),

  sliderInput("Param2", label = "Param 2",

              min =  0,
              max = 10,
              value = 0),

  sliderInput("Param3", label = "Param 3",

              min =  0,
              max = 10,
              value = 0),

  sliderInput("Param4",  label = "Param 4",

              min =  0,
              max = 10,
              value = 0),
  actionButton(inputId = "AutoParam", label = "Find the optimal Param"),

  plotOutput(outputId = "ParamPlot"),
  tableOutput("Criteria")

)

server <- function(input, output, session) {

  RES <- reactive({

    v <- reactiveValues(valueButton = 0)

    # Each time button is click, add 1 to custom value of the button

    MOD2 <- eventReactive(input$AutoParam, {

      v$valueButton = v$valueButton + 1

      Param1 <- 1
      Param2 <- 2
      Param3 <- 3
      Param4 <- 4
      VAL <- Param1 + Param2 + Param3 + Param4
      updateSliderInput(session, inputId = "Param1", value = Param1)
      updateSliderInput(session, inputId = "Param2", value = Param2)
      updateSliderInput(session, inputId = "Param3", value = Param3)
      updateSliderInput(session, inputId = "Param4", value = Param4)
      updateActionButton(session, inputId = "AutoParam", label = "Auto")
      return(list(VAL = VAL))

    })

    # Change on sliderInput

    MOD1 <- eventReactive({input$Param1 ; input$Param2 ; input$Param3 ; input$Param4}, {

      # If change on slider is because of button, v$valueButton==1
      if (v$valueButton == 0) {

        Param1 <- input$Param1
        Param2 <- input$Param2
        Param3 <- input$Param3
        Param4 <- input$Param4
        VAL <- Param1 + Param2 + Param3 + Param4
        updateActionButton(session, inputId = "AutoParam", label = "reactiveValues() in a global reactive()")
        return(list(VAL = VAL))

      }
      # reset value of valueButton

      v$valueButton <- 0
    })

    if (v$valueButton == 0) {
      MOD <- MOD1()$VAL
      isolate(MOD1())
    } else {
      MOD <- MOD2()$VAL
    }

    IDX <- MOD * 2

    return(list(MOD = MOD, IDX = IDX))

  })

  output$ParamPlot <- renderPlot({
    print(str(RES()$MOD))
    plot(RES()$MOD, RES()$MOD, main = "",
         xlim = c(0, 40), ylim = c(0, 40))
  })
  output$Criteria <- renderTable({
    data.frame(Param = c(RES()$MOD, RES()$IDX))
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)

messages.subject: Recording User Audio from Shiny R Server
messages.subject_clean: Recording User Audio from Shiny R Server
messages.body_plain:
I'm writing a shiny app to be run from a linux server. As part of the app I aim to record and playback audio to the user using the audio library:

observeEvent(input$record, {
             # record audio
x <- rep(NA_real_, 44100*2*3) # for 3 seconds
     # start recording into x
wait(record(x, 44100, 2))

# record audio
save.wave(x, paste( input$name,".wav",sep=""))
                       }

# PLAYBACK SOUND
observeEvent(input$play, {
wait(play( v$x ))
})

When running this on my own machine there is no problem, however when running the app from the linux server I get the following:

Listening on http://127.0.0.1:34971
Warning: Error in record: no audio drivers are available
Stack trace (innermost first):
    67: record
    66: wait
    65: observeEventHandler [/srv/shiny-server/ethnoling/app.R#156]
     1: runApp

I was under the impression the server would use the user's audio driver to send and receive audio data to the server. Is that not how it works? Do I need an audio driver on the server too? Sorry, I do statistics in R, I'm not a developer :)

messages.subject: Re: Recording User Audio from Shiny R Server
messages.subject_clean: Recording User Audio from Shiny R Server
messages.body_plain:
No, this isn't going to work--it'll attempt to record *from the server*, meaning, using whatever audio device is on the server. So you'll just get a recording of fan noise or whatever. :-\

In order to record and playback audio from the user, you'll need to use the browser's recording/playback capabilities, which can be done but requires someone to write the JavaScript (both to record/playback the audio and to send it to the Shiny server). This is probably at least a day or two of work for a good JS + Shiny developer, but the result would be reusable by everyone.

messages.subject: Re: New to Rshiny, bootstrapPage question
messages.subject_clean: New to Rshiny, bootstrapPage question
messages.body_plain:
bootstrapPage() creates an empty container (not even a div tag, just a list of HTML tags which happens to have zero elements), with metadata attached to load the Bootstrap CSS and JS assets. If you want to stay in R for defining your UI, you can pass in any HTML objects as children of bootstrapPage.

bootstrapPage(
  tags$div(id = "mainContainer",
    "This is text in the main container"
  ),
  tags$button(class = "btn btn-primary", "Here's a button")
)

Note that when you define your UI in R, you shouldn't insert the outer <html> or <body> tags, those are implied.

You can also write raw HTML if you want, or combine raw HTML with R calls. It should all be described in the video "Shiny UI" by Garrett Grolemund, on this page:
https://www.rstudio.com/resources/webinars/shiny-developer-conference/

messages.body_plain:
I'm new in Shiny and I'm trying to replicate the `pick_points`function from the Shiny [webinars](https://github.com/rstudio/webinars/blob/master/29-Shiny-Gadgets/brush-gadget.R) in a different context.

I've the following data from Twitter which basically contains an ID, date, type of tweet and username.

    tweets <- structure(list(id_str = c(841706677183344640, 841706613656416256,
    841706515484573696, 841706506961715200, 841706475504386048, 841683777638301696,
    841683745971277824, 841683738840948736, 841683727851880448, 841683686290530304,
    841683658146693120, 841664976628662272, 841664957527744512, 841664934442352640,
    841664815798067200, 841664811754745856, 841664757287538688),
        time = structure(c(1489510800, 1489510800, 1489510800, 1489510800,
        1489510800, 1489507200, 1489507200, 1489507200, 1489507200,
        1489507200, 1489507200, 1489500000, 1489500000, 1489500000,
        1489500000, 1489500000, 1489500000), class = c("POSIXct",
        "POSIXt"), tzone = "UTC"), type = structure(c(1L, 2L, 2L,
        1L, 3L, 3L, 2L, 3L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 3L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 2L, 2L), .Label = c("retweet",
        "original", "@mention"), class = "factor"), from_user = c("fixit_fitz",
        "BeingFarhad", "TrumptheClown1", "Book_Blackparad", "Hofmockel",
        "EnergyInnovLLC", "Sarah_Lorya", "momentinthepark", "MommaBjornen68",
        "arevalor514", "ize0", "EPWDems", "SoniaKris13", "SaleemulHuq",
        "manojkumar127in", "maritvp", "channingdutton")), .Names = c("id_str",
    "time", "type", "from_user"), row.names = c(NA, -17L), class = c("tbl_df",
    "tbl", "data.frame"))

I'm using the following code to create a Shiny gadget:

    library(shiny)
    library(miniUI)
    library(tidyverse)

    temporal <- function(tweets) {
        ui <- miniPage(
            gadgetTitleBar("Temporal Analysis"),
            miniTabstripPanel(
                miniTabPanel("Visualize", icon = icon("area-chart"),
                             miniContentPanel(
                                 checkboxInput("checkbox", label = "Type", value = FALSE),
                                 plotOutput("plot1", height = "80%", brush = 'brush')
                             ),
                             miniButtonBlock(
                                actionButton("add", "", icon = icon("thumbs-up")),
                                actionButton("sub", "", icon = icon("thumbs-down")),
                                actionButton("none", "" , icon = icon("ban")),
                                actionButton("all", "", icon = icon("refresh"))
                             )
                ),
                miniTabPanel("Data", icon = icon("table"),
                             miniContentPanel(
                                 DT::dataTableOutput("table")
                             )
                )
            )
        )

        server <- function(input, output) {
            # Cleaning
            data <- tweets %>% select(id_str, time) %>%
                group_by(time) %>%
                summarise(n = n())

            # For storing selected points
            vals <- reactiveValues(keep = rep(TRUE, nrow(data)))

            output$plot1 <- renderPlot({
                # Plot the kept and excluded points as two separate data sets
                keep    <- data[ vals$keep, , drop = FALSE]
                exclude <- data[!vals$keep, , drop = FALSE]

                ggplot(keep, aes(time, n)) +
                    geom_point(data = exclude, color = "grey80") +
                    geom_point(size = 2) +
                    geom_line(data = data)
            })

            # Update selected points
            selected <- reactive({
                brushedPoints(data, input$brush, allRows = TRUE)$selected_
            })
            observeEvent(input$add,  vals$keep <- vals$keep | selected())
            observeEvent(input$sub,  vals$keep <- vals$keep & !selected())
            observeEvent(input$all,  vals$keep <- rep(TRUE, nrow(data)))
            observeEvent(input$none, vals$keep <- rep(FALSE, nrow(data)))

            # Show table
            output$table <- DT::renderDataTable({
                dates <- data$time[vals$keep]
                tweets %>% filter(time %in% dates)
            })

            observeEvent(input$done, {
                dates <- data$time[vals$keep]
                stopApp(tweets %>% filter(time %in% dates))
            })
            observeEvent(input$cancel, {
                stopApp(NULL)
            })

        }

        runGadget(ui, server)
    }

To run it simply write `temporal(tweets)` and it should display this:

 <https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/-jFCIIkw3gRY/WMsqPbtAuSI/AAAAAAAAPL4/StQuG2YaJuIUpAhd9bteUeYpA2mBFN5XACLcB/s1600/Captura%2Bde%2Bpantalla%2B2017-03-17%2Ba%2Bla%2528s%2529%2B0.12.56.png>

However, I want to use a checkbox (it appears in the image top-left corner), i.e. `checkboxInput("checkbox", label = "Type", value = FALSE)`, such that the type of tweet can be included in the plot. This involves a conditional statement:

        data <- reactive({
            if (input$checkbox) {
                tweets %>% select(id_str, time, type) %>%
                    group_by(time, type) %>%
                    summarise(n = n())
            } else {
                tweets %>% select(id_str, time) %>%
                    group_by(time) %>%
                    summarise(n = n())
            }
        })

        # For storing selected points
        valsKeep <- reactive({reactiveValues(keep = rep(TRUE, nrow(data())))})

        output$plot1 <- renderPlot({
            # Plot the kept and excluded points as two separate data sets
            keep    <- data()[ valsKeep(), , drop = FALSE]
            exclude <- data()[!valsKeep(), , drop = FALSE]

            if (input$checkbox) {
                ggplot(keep, aes(time, n, col = type)) +
                    geom_point(data = exclude, color = "grey80") +
                    geom_point(size = 2) +
                    geom_line(data = data()) +
                    scale_colour_brewer(palette = "Dark2")
            } else {
                ggplot(keep, aes(time, n)) +
                    geom_point(data = exclude, color = "grey80") +
                    geom_point(size = 2) +
                    geom_line(data = data())
            }
        })

Basically, the data variable becomes reactive and this influences the reactiveValues in valsKeep and the renderPlot. I know this is not the correct wat to do it, but I'm not completely sure how to proceed.

Any help is greatly appreciated.

messages.subject: Re: how to plot the graph in viewer to shinydashboard?
messages.subject_clean: how to plot the graph in viewer to shinydashboard?
messages.body_plain:
Looks like xgb.plot.tree uses a package called DiagrammeR, which is based on an htmlwidget--that's good.

You can basically do something like this:

In UI:
DiagrammeROutput("plot")

In server function:
output$plot <- renderDiagrammeR({
  ...
  xgb.plot.tree(..., render=FALSE)
})

Make sure you include the render=FALSE argument to xgb.plot.tree when using inside renderDiagrammeR.

messages.subject: Driving me mad - can't get isolate() and server-side updateSelectizeInput() to play nice
messages.subject_clean: Driving me mad - can't get isolate() and server-side updateSelectizeInput() to play nice
messages.body_plain:
I'm building a shiny app where there are some very large input lists to search against (nearly 20,000 genes). So, naturally I want to move the selectize over the server. But this is having annoying behavior when combined with isolate. I use an actionButton() to generate the plot. But when the page first loads, using server-side updateSelectizeInput() results in a null gene (I think) being sent to my plotting function. So an error immediately gets printed on first load. This goes away after clicking the actionButton.

Here's a toy example which (kind of) shows the problem. On inital load the ggplot isn't being plotted for the selected gene. Only when I hit the actionButton does the plot appear. How do I modify this to pass the selected 'gene' to the output$boxPlot on load?

server.R:
library(shiny)
library(tidyverse)

genes <- c('A','B')
expression <- cbind(rbind(10,100),genes) %>% data.frame()
colnames(expression) <- c('Expression','Gene')

shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {
  updateSelectizeInput(session, 'Gene', choices = genes, selected='A', server = TRUE)

  output$boxPlot <- renderPlot({
    input$pan_button
    isolate({
      input.gene <- input$Gene
      plot_data <- expression %>% filter(Gene %in% input.gene)
      ggplot(plot_data, aes(x=Gene,y=as.numeric(as.character(Expression)))) + geom_bar(stat='identity') + ylim(0,100)
    })
  })
})

ui.R
library(shiny)

fluidPage( actionButton('pan_button','Re-draw Plot!'),
           selectizeInput('Gene',strong('Gene:'), choices = NULL, selected='ABCA4'),
           plotOutput('boxPlot'))

messages.subject: Save session data/cookies?
messages.subject_clean: Save session data/cookies?
messages.body_plain:
Hi there,

So I wrote an app that analyzes student loan information and recommends the best way to pay them down. A lot of people, including myself, have multiple student loans with different interest rates, so I made some conditional panels that show up based on how many student loans the user says they have. Each conditional panel has numeric inputs for loan principal, interest rate, and how much the user wants to pay per month. It's a bit of a process to enter all this data once, and unfortunately it all gets wiped out if the user navigates away from the page or refreshes it.

How can I save the session data associated with each numeric input so the user doesn't have to re-enter their information every single time?

Thanks!

messages.subject: Re: How to add observeEvent inside a function?
messages.subject_clean: How to add observeEvent inside a function?
messages.body_plain:
I'll to try to answer as much of your question as I can:

1) The fact that you cannot contain an observer inside a function is because a function is callable, while an observer isn't. You don't call an observer and tell it when to execute -- that's its job. I think you might have been misunderstanding an observer as just a function without return values, but that's not true. While an observer does not return anything, it also isn't callable, so you can't contain it in a callable type, like a function. I don't think this is about environments at all -- that concept isn't even that important for reactive programming, where we usually talk of reactive contexts. Again, however, I don't think this is the problem here.

2) I don't quite understand why you'd want to initialize reactive_ranges inside the function? Isn't that one of the parameters/arguments you pass in? If there is no predetermined value for reactive_ranges, then of course you can create it inside the function and keep it contained in that way.

3) You can use lapply or a similar function to avoid repetition/boilerplate if you have a lot of similar observers.

4) A lot of Shiny "extensions" (like the dt properties and the plot click, brush etc...) were not planned in advanced, so the final spec ends up being a little arbitrary. We don't have any checks to see if all inputs and outputs declared in the UI are used in the server. Part of this is because this isn't always supposed to be so -- if you have dynamic outputs, they'll be present in the server, but not in the UI. If you find that your code is getting unreadable as a consequence, I'd recommend using modules, where it's a lot easier (compered to a large app) to see what goes with what..

messages.body_plain:
Yes, the req() solves one problem. The weirdness I had was because I forgot I was ALSO using some inputs to dynamically resize the plot. So I had to also use req() on that function.

The other problem (having nothing initially loaded), was solved by using if else statements with the actionButtons.

Here's an updated 'solved' toy example:

library(shiny)
library(tidyverse)

genes <- c('A','B','C')
expression <- cbind(rbind(10,100,25),genes) %>% data.frame()

colnames(expression) <- c('Expression','Gene')

load_plot <- ggplot(expression %>% filter(Gene %in% genes[c(1,2)]), aes(x=Gene,y=as.numeric(as.character(Expression)))) + geom_bar(stat='identity') + ylim(0,100)

ui <- fluidPage(
  actionButton('pan_button','Re-draw Plot!'),
  selectizeInput('Gene',strong('Gene:'), choices = NULL, selected='ABCA4', multiple = TRUE),
  plotOutput('boxPlot')
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {

  updateSelectizeInput(session, 'Gene', choices = genes, selected=c('A','B'), server = TRUE)

  output$boxPlot <- renderPlot({
    input$pan_button
    if (input$pan_button==0){load_plot}
    else{

      isolate({
        input.gene <- input$Gene
        plot_data <- expression %>% filter(Gene %in% input.gene)
        ggplot(plot_data, aes(x=Gene,y=as.numeric(as.character(Expression)))) + geom_bar(stat='identity') + ylim(0,100)
      })
    }
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)

messages.body_plain:
How about this?

NumberUI <- function(id){
  ns <- NS(id)

  numericInput(ns("obs"), "Observations:", 1, min = 1, max = 100)

}

Number <- function(input, output, session){

  reactive(input$obs)
}

ui <- fluidPage(

  numericInput("numInputs", "How many inputs do you want", 4),

  uiOutput("inputGroup"),
  textOutput('final')
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  observeEvent(input$numInputs, {
    output$inputGroup = renderUI({
      lapply(1:input$numInputs, function(i) {
        NumberUI(i)
      })
    })
  })

  test <- reactive({
    unlist(lapply(1:input$numInputs, function(i) {
      callModule(Number, as.character(i))()
    }))
  })

  output$final <- renderPrint({
    test()
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)

messages.subject: Re: Clear/Reset fileInput()
messages.subject_clean: Clear/Reset fileInput()
messages.body_plain:
The easiest way around it is to take care of both resetting the fileInput widget AND the underlying data (treat it as two different things). For example:

library(shiny)
library(shinyjs)

ui <- fluidPage(
  useShinyjs(),
  fileInput('inFile', 'Choose file'),
  actionButton('reset', 'Reset'),
  tableOutput('tbl')
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {

  rv <- reactiveValues(data = NULL)

  observe({
    req(input$inFile)
    rv$data <- read.csv(input$inFile$datapath)
  })

  observeEvent(input$reset, {
    rv$data <- NULL
    reset('inFile')
  })

  output$tbl <- renderTable({
    rv$data
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)

1) That is not wrong. In fact, that is exactly what happens if you do this:

# Naive approach (only works once)
ui <- fluidPage(
  radioButtons("rd1", "Radio buttons 1", 1),
  radioButtons("rd2", "Radio buttons 2", 1),
  actionButton("go", "Add choices")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  add_choices <- function(id, choices) {
    observeEvent(input$go, {
      updateRadioButtons(session, id, choices = choices)
    })
  }

  add_choices("rd1", sample(1:100, 3))
  add_choices("rd2", sample(1:100, 3))
}

shinyApp(ui, server)

The problem is that this is probably not what you want to do, since it only "works" the first time around. Since Shiny has its own event loop, the observers created with the app above will always have choices equal to whatever the first vector was. So this approach would only work if you only needed the observer to be called once. And even in though cases, the fact that it doesn't behave as you'd expect is reason enough to discourage its use.

here's what I'd recommend you do instead:

# will be called later)

  radioButtons("rd1", "Radio buttons 1", 1),
  radioButtons("rd2", "Radio buttons 2", 1),
  actionButton("go", "Add choices")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  add_choices <- function(id, choices) {
    updateRadioButtons(session, id, choices = choices)
  }

  ### Option 1: (this is necessary if the triggering events are different)
  # observeEvent(input$go, add_choices("rd1", sample(1:100, 3)))
  # observeEvent(input$go, add_choices("rd2", sample(1:100, 3)))

  ### Option 2: (more conside and good enough for our case)
  observeEvent(input$go, {
    add_choices("rd1", sample(1:100, 3))
    add_choices("rd2", sample(1:100, 3))
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)

3) This gist goes over using lapply vs for loops in Shiny: https://gist.github.com/bborgesr/e1ce7305f914f9ca762c69509dda632e. In case it is of any help :)

messages.body_plain:
Sorry for not weighing in earlier. I think it's quite reasonable to do what was requested in the original message (note that this is the original code verbatim and doesn't work):

 add_zoom <- function(plot_id, reactive_ranges) {
  reactive_ranges <<- c(x = NULL, y = NULL)
  observeEvent(input[[paste0(plot_id, "_dblclick")]], {
    brush <- input[[paste0(plot_id, "_brush")]]
    if (!is.null(brush)) {
      reactive_ranges$x <<- c(brush$xmin, brush$xmax)
      reactive_ranges$y <<- c(brush$ymin, brush$ymax)
    } else {
      reactive_ranges$x <<- NULL
      reactive_ranges$y <<- NULL
    }
  })
}
add_zoom("location_plot_gg", values$location_plot_gg_ranges)

It's totally fine to call observeEvent inside of functions. However, there is a bug in the way the `values$location_plot_gg_ranges` is passed and then assigned to--the <<- operator doesn't nearly do what you're expecting it to here, nor would you want it to. It's almost like you're trying to pass `values$location_plot_gg_ranges` "by reference", as we'd say in C; you can't do that, but you can pass `values` itself by reference.

You could do this instead:

add_zoom <- function(plot_id, rvalues, slot) {
  rvalues[[slot]] <- list(x = NULL, y = NULL)

  observeEvent(input[[paste0(plot_id, "_dblclick")]], {
    brush <- input[[paste0(plot_id, "_brush")]]
    if (!is.null(brush)) {

      rvalues[[slot]]$x <- c(brush$xmin, brush$xmax)
      rvalues[[slot]]$y <- c(brush$ymin, brush$ymax)
    } else {
      rvalues[[slot]]$x <- NULL
      rvalues[[slot]]$y <- NULL
    }
  })
}
add_zoom("location_plot_gg", values, "location_plot_gg_ranges")

but the add_zoom API is then a little strange, in that you're passing a reactive values object and slot name in. Since the ranges value will not be overwritten by anyone else (right?) we could simplify the add_zoom API by having it return a reactive expression:

add_zoom <- function(plot_id) {
  rv <- reactiveValues(range = list(x = NULL, y = NULL))

  observeEvent(input[[paste0(plot_id, "_dblclick")]], {
    brush <- input[[paste0(plot_id, "_brush")]]
    if (!is.null(brush)) {

      rv$range$x <- c(brush$xmin, brush$xmax)
      rv$range$y <- c(brush$ymin, brush$ymax)
    } else {
      rv$range$x <- NULL
      rv$range$y <- NULL
    }
  })
  reactive(rv$range)
}
location_plot_gg_range <- add_zoom("location_plot_gg", values, "location_plot_gg_ranges")

Then elsewhere in your UI you can use location_plot_gg_range() to reactively read the brushed range.

By the way, you're coming pretty close to Shiny Modules at this point... https://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/modules.html

Hope this helps.

messages.body_plain:
Hi Joe,

Thanks so much for the reply! Your solutions are really smart.

So the first version passed the components needed to reference the value in variables, then the dynamically assembled expression access the value we want directly.

Then the second version focused on the reactive value of "range" and return it only, with the observeEvent happened as side effect. In this way we don't even need a global reactive value to hold the range, since it's just some operations applied to brush values.

Though that lead me to think maybe we don't need the extra layer of rv$range, and we also don't need the reactive wrapper. I put all versions in same app to test it, the plot 5 with my modifications seemed work, but I'm not sure if there is any problem with it.

full code below, also in attachment if that is easier to copy
-----------------------------
library(ggplot2)
library(shiny)

options(shiny.trace = TRUE)

ui <- fluidPage(
  fluidRow(
    column(width = 4, class = "well",
      h4("zoom1"),
      plotOutput("plot1", height = 300,
        dblclick = "plot1_dblclick",
        brush = brushOpts(
          id = "plot1_brush",
          resetOnNew = TRUE
        )
      )
    ),
    column(width = 4, class = "well",
      h4("zoom2"),
      plotOutput("plot2", height = 300,
        dblclick = "plot2_dblclick",
        brush = brushOpts(
          id = "plot2_brush",
          resetOnNew = TRUE
        )
      )
    ),
    column(width = 4, class = "well",
      h4("zoom3"),
      plotOutput("plot3", height = 300,
        dblclick = "plot3_dblclick",
        brush = brushOpts(
          id = "plot3_brush",
          resetOnNew = TRUE
        )
      )
    )
  ),
  fluidRow(
    column(width = 4, class = "well",
      h4("zoom4"),
      plotOutput("plot4", height = 300,
        dblclick = "plot4_dblclick",
        brush = brushOpts(
          id = "plot4_brush",
          resetOnNew = TRUE
        )
      )
    ),
    column(width = 4, class = "well",
    h4("zoom5"),
    plotOutput("plot5", height = 300,
      dblclick = "plot5_dblclick",
      brush = brushOpts(
        id = "plot5_brush",
        resetOnNew = TRUE
      )
    )
  )
  )
)

server <- function(input, output) {
  # plot 1, add zoom with regular approach ----
  values <- reactiveValues()
  values$plot1_ranges <- reactiveValues(x = NULL, y = NULL)

  output$plot1 <- renderPlot({
    ggplot(mtcars, aes(wt, mpg)) +
      geom_point() +
      coord_cartesian(xlim = values$plot1_ranges$x, ylim = values$plot1_ranges$y)
  })

  # When a double-click happens, check if there's a brush on the plot.
  # If so, zoom to the brush bounds; if not, reset the zoom.
  observeEvent(input$plot1_dblclick, {
    brush <- input$plot1_brush
    if (!is.null(brush)) {
      values$plot1_ranges$x <- c(brush$xmin, brush$xmax)
      values$plot1_ranges$y <- c(brush$ymin, brush$ymax)

    } else {
      values$plot1_ranges$x <- NULL
      values$plot1_ranges$y <- NULL
    }
  })

  # plot 2, call function in observeEvent expression parameter ----
  values$plot2_ranges <- reactiveValues(x = NULL, y = NULL)

  add_zoom <- function(plot_id, reactive_ranges) {
    brush <- input[[paste0(plot_id, "_brush")]]
    if (!is.null(brush)) {
      reactive_ranges$x <- c(brush$xmin, brush$xmax)
      reactive_ranges$y <- c(brush$ymin, brush$ymax)
    } else {
      reactive_ranges$x <- NULL
      reactive_ranges$y <- NULL
    }
  }

  output$plot2 <- renderPlot({
    ggplot(mtcars, aes(wt, mpg)) +
      geom_point() +
      coord_cartesian(xlim = values$plot2_ranges$x, ylim = values$plot2_ranges$y)
  })
  observeEvent(input$plot2_dblclick, add_zoom("plot2", values$plot2_ranges))

  # plot 3, use varialbe$slot separately ----
  add_zoom_slot <- function(plot_id, rvalues, slot) {

    rvalues[[slot]] <- list(x = NULL, y = NULL)
    observeEvent(input[[paste0(plot_id, "_dblclick")]], {
      brush <- input[[paste0(plot_id, "_brush")]]
      if (!is.null(brush)) {
        rvalues[[slot]]$x <- c(brush$xmin, brush$xmax)
        rvalues[[slot]]$y <- c(brush$ymin, brush$ymax)
      } else {
        rvalues[[slot]]$x <- NULL
        rvalues[[slot]]$y <- NULL
      }
    })
  }

  output$plot3 <- renderPlot({
    ggplot(mtcars, aes(wt, mpg)) +
      geom_point() +
      coord_cartesian(xlim = values$plot3_ranges$x, ylim = values$plot3_ranges$y)
  })
  add_zoom_slot("plot3", values, "plot3_ranges")
  # plot 4, reactive expression ----
  add_zoom_exp <- function(plot_id) {

    rv <- reactiveValues(range = list(x = NULL, y = NULL))
    observeEvent(input[[paste0(plot_id, "_dblclick")]], {
      brush <- input[[paste0(plot_id, "_brush")]]
      if (!is.null(brush)) {
        rv$range$x <- c(brush$xmin, brush$xmax)
        rv$range$y <- c(brush$ymin, brush$ymax)
      } else {
        rv$range$x <- NULL
        rv$range$y <- NULL
      }
    })
    reactive(rv$range)
  }

  plot4_range <- add_zoom_exp("plot4")

  output$plot4 <- renderPlot({
    ggplot(mtcars, aes(wt, mpg)) +
      geom_point() +
      coord_cartesian(xlim = plot4_range()$x, ylim = plot4_range()$y)
  })
  # plot 5, reactive expression with less level ----
  add_zoom_exp_2 <- function(plot_id) {
    ranges <- reactiveValues(x = NULL, y = NULL)

    observeEvent(input[[paste0(plot_id, "_dblclick")]], {
      brush <- input[[paste0(plot_id, "_brush")]]
      if (!is.null(brush)) {

        ranges$x <- c(brush$xmin, brush$xmax)
        ranges$y <- c(brush$ymin, brush$ymax)
      } else {
        ranges$x <- NULL
        ranges$y <- NULL
      }
    })
    ranges
  }
  plot5_range <- add_zoom_exp_2("plot5")
  output$plot5 <- renderPlot({
    ggplot(mtcars, aes(wt, mpg)) +
      geom_point() +
      coord_cartesian(xlim = plot5_range$x, ylim = plot5_range$y)
  })

}
shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)

After reading more carefully, I believe Joe's version should be the idiomatic way. My plot5 works because ranges happened to hold x and y reactive values. ranges itself is not reactive so we don't need to wrap with reactive() in return expression, the usage of ranges$x accessed the reactive value part.

So if we write a zoom that only zoom in x axis and return the x part directly, we will need to use the reactive() expression:

-----
  # plot 6, reactive value ----
  add_zoom_exp_3 <- function(plot_id) {

    ranges <- reactiveValues(x = NULL, y = NULL)
    observeEvent(input[[paste0(plot_id, "_dblclick")]], {
      brush <- input[[paste0(plot_id, "_brush")]]
      if (!is.null(brush)) {
        ranges$x <- c(brush$xmin, brush$xmax)
        ranges$y <- c(brush$ymin, brush$ymax)
      } else {
        ranges$x <- NULL
        ranges$y <- NULL
      }
    })

    reactive(ranges$x)
  }
  plot6_range_x <- add_zoom_exp_3("plot6")
  output$plot6 <- renderPlot({

    ggplot(mtcars, aes(wt, mpg)) +
      geom_point() +

      coord_cartesian(xlim = plot6_range_x())
  })

By the way I do intend to read more about modules, which should be the way to go since I will have a lot of plots and adding many similar features to them.

messages.subject_clean: R shiny: Check if some download is available to the user
messages.body_plain:
Oh, you were asking whether the *uploaded* file was there, and based on that, whether to enable/disable the *download* button? (I assume you're saying there's nothing to download if nothing's been uploaded?)

isFileThere <- reactive(is.null(input$file1))
observe({
  if (isFileThere()) {
    shinyjs::enable("download1")
  } else {
    shinyjs::disable("download1")
  }
})

shinyjs::disable is an operation that has a side effect, and therefore doesn't belong in a reactive(), but instead in an observe(). I talk about this in the videos about Effective Reactive Programming on this page <https://www.rstudio.com/resources/webinars/shiny-developer-conference/> (it's a couple of hours long but quite essential information if you're serious about writing Shiny apps).

I only skimmed this thread but this jumped out at me:

  observeEvent(input$numInputs, {
    output$inputGroup = renderUI({
      lapply(1:input$numInputs, function(i) {
        NumberUI(i)
      })
    })
  })

should just be:

    output$inputGroup <- renderUI({
      lapply(1:input$numInputs, NumberUI)
    })

The main thing is the observeEvent going away, the simplification of lapply is just a nice bonus (assuming it works, I haven't actually run this code).

messages.subject: Re: Set outputOptions for all outputs of a module from parent application
messages.subject_clean: Set outputOptions for all outputs of a module from parent application
messages.body_plain:
I just realized this can be worked around today by using an observer to inspect names(session$clientData):

unsuspendAll <- function(session = getDefaultReactiveDomain()) {
  observe({
    pattern <- "^output_(.*?)_hidden$"

    ids <- names(session$clientData) %>%
      grep(pattern, ., value = TRUE) %>%
      sub(pattern, "\\1", .)
    for (id in ids) {
      print(id)
      outputOptions(session$output, id, suspendWhenHidden = FALSE)
    }
  })
}

Define this function in global.R or at the top of server.R or app.R, and call it from inside of your app's server function. As written, it will apply to *all* outputs of your app--past, present, and future. You can tweak/extend it if you'd like to limit it to particular modules or whatever.

Note that I originally tried testing this on plotOutput/renderPlot. plotOutput presents a second challenge: even if suspendWhenHidden=FALSE, by default, renderPlot will try to set the plot output size to the same width/height of the plotOutput, which will be 0 by 0 pixels when it's not actually visible. You can work around this if necessary by providing explicit width and height arguments to the renderPlot() function call itself (NOT the call to plotOutput and not any function calls inside the renderPlot code block). For example, renderPlot({...}, width=400, height=300).

messages.subject_clean: Updating file list after deleting a file
messages.body_plain:
updateSelectInput is how you do it. If it's not working, we'll need to see what code you tried and whether there were any errors.

This is extremely dangerous code though. A malicious user could set literally any value for input$filedelete, just by popping open the JavaScript console and writing Shiny.onInputChange("filedelete", "C:\\AUTOEXEC.BAT") or whatever. At the very least you need to verify that the value of input$filedelete is a file they should actually be able to delete.

Also, you might consider adding an action button to perform the actual deletion, so they have to select a file and then explicitly hit a Delete button. You can do that with an observeEvent() instead of an observe().

> Andras
>
> On Tue, Mar 21, 2017 at 6:18 AM Joe Cheng <j...@rstudio.com> wrote:
> > I just realized this can be worked around today by using an observer to inspect names(session$clientData):
> >
> > unsuspendAll <- function(session = getDefaultReactiveDomain()) {
> >   observe({
> >     pattern <- "^output_(.*?)_hidden$"
> >
> >     ids <- names(session$clientData) %>%
> >       grep(pattern, ., value = TRUE) %>%
> >       sub(pattern, "\\1", .)
> >     for (id in ids) {
> >       print(id)
> >       outputOptions(session$output, id, suspendWhenHidden = FALSE)
> >     }
> >   })
> > }
> >
> > Define this function in global.R or at the top of server.R or app.R, and call it from inside of your app's server function. As written, it will apply to *all* outputs of your app--past, present, and future. You can tweak/extend it if you'd like to limit it to particular modules or whatever.
> >
> > Note that I originally tried testing this on plotOutput/renderPlot. plotOutput presents a second challenge: even if suspendWhenHidden=FALSE, by default, renderPlot will try to set the plot output size to the same width/height of the plotOutput, which will be 0 by 0 pixels when it's not actually visible. You can work around this if necessary by providing explicit width and height arguments to the renderPlot() function call itself (NOT the call to plotOutput and not any function calls inside the renderPlot code block). For example, renderPlot({...}, width=400, height=300).
> >
> > On Mon, Mar 20, 2017 at 10:32 AM Andrew Sali <sali....@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > Hi Barbara,
> > >
> > > Thanks very much for your reply! That is indeed a solution for the case when you are in control of the module development as well. In our current workflow however, some people (potentially relatively new to Shiny) are contributing by creating analysis modules, whilst others are purely writing wrappers around them for a larger application.
> > >
> > > So it's somewhat less feasible to ask them to write an extra handler reactive for each module unfortunately.
> > >
> > > I will be following the github issue then, thanks for the pointer!
> > >
> > > Best,
> > >
> > > Andras
> > >
> > >
> > > On Monday, March 20, 2017 at 4:57:31 PM UTC+1, Bárbara Borges wrote:
> > > > It would be nice to be able to set stuff like this from the parent application. I'm adding this question to an existing Shiny Github issue along similar lines (https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/issues/1546). Maybe we'll have a better answer in the future! For now, here's another way. Basically, you can pass a reactive from the parent to the module as an argument, specifying the wanted value for suspendWhenHidden. On the module, you set an observer for this reactive, and alter the outputOptions accordingly.
> > > >
> > > > library(shiny)
> > > >
> > > > modUI <- function(id) {
> > > >   ns <- NS(id)
> > > >   tagList(
> > > >     plotOutput(ns("p1")),
> > > >     plotOutput(ns("p2"))
> > > >   )
> > > > }
> > > > mod <- function(input, output, session, numPoints, suspendWhenHidden) {
> > > >   observe({
> > > >     if (!suspendWhenHidden()) {  # when susppendWhenHidden = FALSE
> > > >       outputOptions(output, "p1", suspendWhenHidden = FALSE)
> > > >       outputOptions(output, "p2", suspendWhenHidden = FALSE)
> > > >     } else { # when susppendWhenHidden = TRUE
> > > >       outputOptions(output, "p1", suspendWhenHidden = TRUE)
> > > >       outputOptions(output, "p2", suspendWhenHidden = TRUE)
> > > >     }
> > > >   })
> > > >
> > > >   output$p1 <- renderPlot({
> > > >     Sys.sleep(1)
> > > >     plot(runif(numPoints()))
> > > >   })
> > > >
> > > >   output$p2 <- renderPlot({
> > > >     Sys.sleep(1)
> > > >     plot(runif(numPoints()))
> > > >   })
> > > > }
> > > >
> > > > ui <- fixedPage(
> > > >   checkboxInput("suspendWhenHidden", "suspendWhenHidden", value = TRUE),
> > > >   tabsetPanel(
> > > >     tabPanel("Module", modUI("modID")),
> > > >     tabPanel("Other stuff", numericInput("points", "How many point to plot", 10))
> > > >   )
> > > > )
> > > >
> > > > server <- function(input, output, session) {
> > > >   callModule(mod, "modID", reactive(input$points), reactive(input$suspendWhenHidden))
> > > > }
> > > >
> > > > shinyApp(ui, server)
> > > >
> > > >
> > > >
> > > > On Monday, March 6, 2017 at 2:20:32 PM UTC, Andrew Sali wrote:
> > > > > Hi,
> > > > >
> > > > > I would like to set the outputOptions of all the outputs of a module that I call in a parent application. In particular, I would like to toggle the suspendWhenHidden flag for all outputs. The motivation is that I would like to pre-calculate certain things before the user continues to the next step (which is hidden and thus Shiny suspends the outputs by default).
> > > > >
> > > > > My problem is that by design the outputs of the module are not directly accessible from the parent application. However controlling the suspendWhenHidden option would still be important for the parent application and thus the decision whether to suspend could be left with the parent application I think.
> > > > >
> > > > > The following "hack" seems to work, however I was wondering if anyone is aware of a more elegant and potentially more robust solution.
> > > > >
> > > > > suspendModuleWhenHidden <- function(output,session,id,suspendWhenHidden=TRUE) {
> > > > >   ns <- session$ns
> > > > >   output_names <- session$clientData %>%
> > > > >     reactiveValuesToList() %>%
> > > > >     names %>%
> > > > >     {.[grepl(NS(ns(id))(""),.,fixed=TRUE)]} %>%
> > > > >     {gsub("^output[_]","",.,fixed=FALSE)} %>%
> > > > >     {gsub("[_]hidden$","",.,fixed=FALSE)} %>%
> > > > >     {gsub(NS(ns(id))(""),"",.,fixed=TRUE)}
> > > > >
> > > > >   for (output_id in output_names) {
> > > > >     try({outputOptions(output,gsub(ns(""),"",NS(ns(id))(output_id),fixed=TRUE),suspendWhenHidden=suspendWhenHidden)},silent = TRUE)
> > > > >   }
> > > > >   return(0)
> > > > > }
> > > > >
> > > > > Any assistance is very much appreciated.
> > > > >
> > > > > Thank you,
> > > > >
> > > > > Andras

messages.subject: Subsetting rules from apriori algorithm doesn´t work
messages.subject_clean: Subsetting rules from apriori algorithm doesn´t work
messages.body_plain:
Hello guys. I know it could be "trivial" but I can´t get it.

I Have a shiny App which I use to make some market basket analysis. The situation is that I am trying to get only a subset of the rules produced by the apriori algorithm. The variables for which I should subset the rules are shown when I select the "Filtrar" option (conditionalPanel) and once I select one or several options, the LHS (left hand side) of the rules should be filtered. How could I get rules only with LHS containing what I choose in "Lado Izquierdo".

Additionaly, I wonder where should I read my csv file? Is it correct where I am reading my dataset?

Any help will be appreciated.

My code is as follow and I attach a sample of my dataset.

setwd("C:/Users/User/Documents/4.- Pentaho")
library(plyr)
library(dplyr)
library(arules)
library(plotly)
transactions_todos <- read.csv("data_rules.csv", sep=";")
for(i in 1:ncol(transactions_todos)){transactions_todos[,i]<-as.factor(transactions_todos[,i])}
ui<-fluidPage(
  titlePanel(title = "My App"),
  sidebarLayout(
    sidebarPanel(
            radioButtons("filtro1","Definir reglas:",
                   c('Todas',
                     'Filtrar'), selected = 'Todas', inline = TRUE),
      conditionalPanel("input.filtro1 === 'Filtrar'",
                       checkboxGroupInput("opcs","Lado Izquierdo:",
                                          choices = colnames(transactions_todos)[1:4],
                                          selected = colnames(transactions_todos)[1], inline = TRUE)),

      checkboxGroupInput("anio","Seleccione un Año:", as.character(levels(transactions_todos$YEAR)),
                         selected = as.character(levels(transactions_todos$YEAR)), inline = TRUE),
      checkboxGroupInput("tienda","Seleccione una Tienda:", as.character(levels(transactions_todos$STORE)),
                         selected = as.character(levels(transactions_todos$STORE)), inline = TRUE),
      checkboxGroupInput("cliente","Seleccione un grupo de Cliente:", as.character(levels(transactions_todos$CUSTOMER)),
                         selected = as.character(levels(transactions_todos$CUSTOMER)), inline = TRUE),
      checkboxGroupInput("categoria","Seleccione una Categoria:", as.character(levels(transactions_todos$CATEGORY)),
                         selected = as.character(levels(transactions_todos$CATEGORY)), inline = TRUE),
      sliderInput("maxlg","Máxima longitud de las reglas:",
                  min=2, max = 10, value = 5, step = 1),
            sliderInput("lgregla","Cantidad de reglas a mostrar:",
                  min=1, max = 15, value = 7, step = 1),

      sliderInput("soporte","Soporte Mínimo:",
                  min=0, max = 1, value = 0.3, step = 0.1),
      sliderInput("confianza","Confianza Mínima:",
                  min=0, max = 1, value = 0.3, step = 0.1)
    ),
    mainPanel(
      tabsetPanel(
        tabPanel("Reglas",
                 dataTableOutput('contents')),
        tabPanel("Gráfico",
                 plotlyOutput("Barras"),
                 br(),
                 br(),
                 dataTableOutput('muestrav')),
        tabPanel("Data",
                 dataTableOutput('tabla'))
      )
    )
  )
)

server<-function(input, output, session) {
  library(plyr)
  library(dplyr)
  library(arules)
  transactions_todos <- read.csv("data_rules.csv", sep=";")
  for(i in 1:ncol(transactions_todos)){transactions_todos[,i]<-as.factor(transactions_todos[,i])}
    tableData <- reactive({
    df<-filter(transactions_todos, YEAR==input$anio & STORE==input$tienda & CUSTOMER==input$cliente & CATEGORY==input$categoria)
    tr<-as(df,"transactions")
    reglas_todos<-apriori(tr, parameter = list(minlen=2,maxlen= input$maxlg, maxtime=10,supp = input$soporte, conf = input$confianza,target = "rules"))
    reglas_todos<- subset(reglas_todos, subset = lift > 1)
    reglas_todos<-reglas_todos[!is.redundant(reglas_todos, measure="lift")]
    reglas_todos<-sort(reglas_todos, by=c("lift", "supp"))

    if(input$filtro1 == 'Filtrar'){
      varsL <- character()
      for(i in 1:length(input$opcs)){
        tmp <- with(transactions_todos, paste(input$opcs[i]))
        varsL <- c(varsL, tmp)
      }
      ##### HERE IS WHERE I AM NOT ABLE TO SUBSET MY RULES
      ar <- subset(reglas_todos, subset=lhs %pin% input$opcs)
      rules_df<-as(ar, "data.frame")
      df_reglas<-data.frame(Antecedente = labels(lhs(reglas_todos), setStart = "", setEnd = ""),
                            Consecuente = labels(rhs(reglas_todos), setStart = "", setEnd = ""),
                            Regla= rules_df$rules,
                            Soporte=round(rules_df$support,4),
                            Confianza=round(rules_df$confidence,4),
                            Lift=round(rules_df$lift,4))
      df_reglas$Antecedente<-gsub(",",", ",df_reglas$Antecedente)
      df_reglas$Consecuente<-gsub(",",", ",df_reglas$Consecuente)
      df_reglas$Regla<-gsub(",",", ",df_reglas$Regla)
      df_reglas[,-c(3)]
    }
    else {
      rules_df<-as(reglas_todos, "data.frame")
      df_reglas<-data.frame(Antecedente = labels(lhs(reglas_todos), setStart = "", setEnd = ""),
                            Consecuente = labels(rhs(reglas_todos), setStart = "", setEnd = ""),
                            Regla= rules_df$rules,
                            Soporte=round(rules_df$support,4),
                            Confianza=round(rules_df$confidence,4),
                            Lift=round(rules_df$lift,4))
      df_reglas$Antecedente<-gsub(",",", ",df_reglas$Antecedente)
      df_reglas$Consecuente<-gsub(",",", ",df_reglas$Consecuente)
      df_reglas$Regla<-gsub(",",", ",df_reglas$Regla)
      df_reglas[,-c(3)]
    }
  })
  output$contents <- renderDataTable({
    reg<-tableData()

  })
  br()
  br()
  output$muestrav<-renderDataTable({
    reg<-tableData()
    rules_df<-as(reg, "data.frame")
    rules_df$Regla<-paste(rules_df$Antecedente, rules_df$Consecuente, sep = " => ")
    rules_df<-rules_df[c(1:input$lgregla),c(1:5)]
  })
  output$tabla<-renderDataTable({
    reg<-tableData()
    rules_df<-as(reg, "data.frame")
    rules_df<-rules_df[c(1:input$lgregla),c(1:5)]
  })
}
shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)

messages.subject: Question : what is the appropriate way to extend checkboxGroupInput to support titatoggle.css
messages.subject_clean: Question : what is the appropriate way to extend checkboxGroupInput to support titatoggle.css
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I've had a little luck extending checkboxGroupInput for my own needs.

I'm pretty sure this is an inelegant way to approach extending checkboxGroupInput ... I will say that it does indeed work

from input-checkboxgroup.R

I have my own divClass as such:

#divClass <- "form-group shiny-input-checkboxgroup shiny-input-container"
divClass <-
"form-group checkbox checkbox-slider--b shiny-input-checkboxgroup shiny-input-container"

and I return a css with the div as such:
# return label and select tag
#tags$div(id = inputId,
#         style = if (!is.null(width)) paste0("width: ", shiny::validateCssUnit(width), ";"),
#         class = divClass,
#         controlLabel(inputId, label),
#         options
#)
tagList(
  shiny::singleton(shiny::tags$head(
    shiny::tags$link(rel = "stylesheet", type = "text/css", href = "titatoggle-dist.css")
  )),
  div(
    id = inputId,
    style = if (!is.null(width))
      paste0("width: ", shiny::validateCssUnit(width), ";"),
    class = divClass,
    controlLabel(inputId, label),
    options
  )
)

I then include the titatoggle-dist.css in my www folder and it seems to work just fine. I just think there must be a better way than modifying the existing shiny source code or cut/copying/pasting non exported functions? Or is this how one would go about extending an existing input source?

I saw some examples here but https://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/building-inputs.html not seeing or understanding the connection

messages.subject: ggplot not working in shiny
messages.subject_clean: ggplot not working in shiny
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone-
I am trying to plot this SIR function according to user-inputted variables. The program runs and the sliders show up, but I can't figure out how to get the plot to display. The issue seems to be with the ggplot command. I included both the UI and server components below. Any help would be appreciated, thanks!!!

library(shiny)
shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(
  headerPanel("Vaccination Modeling"),

    sidebarPanel(
    sliderInput(inputId="p",
                label="Vaccination Rate",
                value=0.1, min=0, max=1),
    sliderInput(inputId="S",
                 label="Initial Susceptible Population",
                 value=500, min=0, max=1000, step=10),
    sliderInput(inputId="I",
                 label="Initial Infected Population",
                 value=200, min=0, max=1000, step=10),
    sliderInput(inputId="R",
                label="Initial Recovered Population",
                value=300, min=0, max=1000, step=10),
    sliderInput(inputId="beta",
                label="Transmission Rate",
                value=0.001, min=0, max=0.2, step=0.00001),
    sliderInput(inputId="gamma",
                label="Recovery Rate",
                value=0.1, min=0, max=1, step=0.05),
    sliderInput(inputId="mu",
                label="Combined Birth/Death Rate",
                value=0.0001, min=0, max=1, step=0.00005),
    sliderInput(inputId="time",
                label="Time",
                value=50, min=1, max=100, step=1)
    ),

mainPanel(
  plotOutput("vacPlot")
  )
))

library(shiny)
library(deSolve)
library(ggplot2)

shinyServer(function(input, output){

  solveSirvac<-function(pars, times=tout){
  sirvac <- function(time, init, pars) {
    with(as.list(c(init, pars)), {
      dS <- ((1-p)*mu*(S+I+R))-(beta * S * I)-(mu*S)
      dI <- beta * S * I - ((gamma+mu) * I)
      dR <- (gamma * I)-(mu*R)+(p*mu*(S+I+R))

      return(list(c(dS, dI, dR)))
    }
    )
  }
  init<-c(S=input$S, I=input$I, R=input$R)
  return(ode(y= init, times = times, func = sirvac, parms = pars))
  }

  output$vacPlot<-renderPlot(function(){
  tout <- seq(0, time=input$time, by = 1)
  guess_pars<-c(beta=input$beta, gamma=input$gamma, mu=input$mu, p=input$p)
  guess<-as.data.frame(solveSirvac(guess_pars, tout))

  print(ggplot(as.data.frame(guess), aes(x=time, y=N, color=s))+geom_line())

  })

})

messages.subject: Google chart resize when browser size change
messages.subject_clean: Google chart resize when browser size change
messages.body_plain:
I know that when we use plotoutplot, we can set height and weight to "auto". Then the plot will resize automatically when the size of the windows change.

But I am using google chart, I'll need to use htmlOutput, which won't resize the chart automatically.

I figured out a way to do this:
1. Create a fake bar plot, and set the height = 0.1, so the plot won't show up.
2. Then I use session$clientData$output_barplot_width in rendergvis:

```
output$image_pie <- renderGvis({
    session$clientData$output_fakeplot_width
    gvisPieChart(data(), labelvar = "Image", numvar = "count",
                 options = list( height = 500))
  })

```

This works nice on my first tabpage. But when I tried to do the same thing in my second tabpage, it won't work. The google chart won't show up. Then I somehow add something and move something unimportant, it works.
Now I am creating my third tabpage, this problem happen again....... It works sometimes when you move something in the layout.....

Is there anyone know what happen? Or other better way to achieve this?

Thanks!

messages.body_plain:
You forgot to call ns() on the inner module.

Change the build_test_set function to this (difference highlighted)

build_test_set <- function(input, output, session) {

  ns <- session$ns   # move this to the top level
  output$test_building_setup_menu <- renderUI({

    numericInput(ns("test_building_setup"), label = "Amount of Tests", value = 4, min = 1, max = 10, step = 1)
  })

  output$test_parameters_master <- renderUI({
    req(input$test_building_setup)

    lapply(1:(as.numeric(input$test_building_setup)), FUN = function(i) {

      create_test_shinyUI(ns(paste0("test_setup_", i)), paste("Test", i))  # call ns() here

    })
  })

  observe({
    req(input$test_building_setup)
    sapply(1:(as.numeric(input$test_building_setup)), function(i) {
      callModule(create_test_shiny, paste0("test_setup_", i))
    })
  })
}

Then everything should work fine. When nesting modules, you cannot forget to call ns() on the id param when you call the inner function's UI component: https://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/modules.html#nesting-modules

messages.subject: shiny::debounce problem with numericInputs and dynamic slider
messages.subject_clean: shiny::debounce problem with numericInputs and dynamic slider
messages.body_plain:
Greetings Shiny users,

I have an app that contains a couple of numericInputs which define the lower and upper limits for a dynamic slider created via renderUI (and the median of those values is used as the value set in the slider).  Since the app is being viewed on touch devices, the customers like being able to hit the little up/down arrows to change the values without having to finger-type the numbers.  I'd like to ensure that the slider is not re-generated unless the user stops hitting up/down on either of these inputs for at least a full second, so this seemed like a perfect opportunity to use the new debounce function from shiny 1.0.  But it seems I am not using the concept correctly because the slider is still getting updated immediately after each press of those arrows.  The code is below and you can run this directly via shiny::runGist("910e6f4a1a02e71f0852ebeda7c31d6c") .  Any ideas of how to get the behavior I'm looking for?  This is running shiny version 1.0.0 (CRAN release).  If you need additional details I'd be glad to provide them.  Thanks in advance!

App code:

library(shiny)

ui <- fluidPage(
   fluidRow(
     numericInput(
       "obs_low",
       "Minimum obs",
       value = 1000,
       min = 500,
       max = 5000,
       step = 100
     ),
     numericInput(
       "obs_max",
       "Maximum obs",
       value = 4000,
       min = 500,
       max = 10000,
       step = 100
     ),
     uiOutput("likely_ui")
   )
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  output$likely_ui <- renderUI({

    # obtain the min and max obs
    min_obs <- input$obs_low
    max_obs <- input$obs_max

    median_obs <- reactive({
      median(c(input$obs_low, input$obs_max))
    })

    min_obs_d <- reactive({ input$obs_low }) %>% debounce(1000)
    max_obs_d <- reactive({ input$obs_max }) %>% debounce(1000)
    median_obs_d <- debounce(median_obs, 1000)

    validate(
      need(min_obs < max_obs, "Minimum obs must be less than maximum obs!")
    )
    tagList(
      sliderInput(
        "prev_likely",
        "Most Likely obs",
        min = min_obs_d(),
        max = max_obs_d(),
        value = median_obs_d(),
        sep = ","
      )
    )
  })
}

shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)

Regards,
Eric
